dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: If clocks are the score of time's song, then what can I do for it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to use this Crafting Bench.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Clocks — or to be more precisely, exquisite clockwork-powered clocks — are our family craft, famous throughout Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Have you heard of the Lady of the Lake's Tear?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: That was the name Lady Furina gave to one of my works.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: What a lovely name, like a song that encapsulates such sadness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A lover of poetry, are we...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Haha, yes, that unsightly attempt of mine. Now, I do not hate my work, but I also love poetry and song.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: My elder brother has gone on to live his own life, while I inherited the family business.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: It's quite unadventurous and unromantic of me, but I do not desire that this craft be lost.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: No worries. May time's song remember you.
